summary: Cloned SMBIOS serial persists after depot reimage and causes MS Office activation failures
description:
Issue summary: After depot reimaging (standard SCCM task sequence) some laptops are failing Microsoft 365 activation. Impact: Users receive 'activation required' prompts and feature restrictions; several reimaged assets show duplicate hardware IDs in inventory. Scope: ~12 devices across two depot runs (US-west depot). This appears to correlate with a cloning step in our vendor's depot workflow that leaves SMBIOS serial and UUID identical across images.

Initial customer-impact: Internal users returned devices with the expectation of a clean image; instead they could not sign into Office apps without re-activation and required manually re-running Microsoft Activation Diagnostics. That is interrupting new-hire setup and returning devices to depot for additional work, delaying onboarding.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Vendor depot image machine using current golden image via USB cloning station
2) Boot machine into Windows, join to corp network, complete SCCM OOBE task sequence, install corp policies
3) Sign in with corp account and open Outlook/Word to trigger Microsoft 365 activation
4) Observe activation prompt or error 'We couldn't activate Office on this device'.
5) Inspect SMBIOS serial with wmic csproduct get uuid, identifying duplicated UUID across two different machines
logs: Office Activation error: 0x8004FC12 - Device identity mismatch
SCCM client logs (ccmexec): 'Hardware inventory upload: Asset tag: 01-ABCD',
comments: Maya Thompson (IT): Reported after three new hires failed to activate Office post-depot; attached asset list and sample wmic output.
Liam Chen (Imaging): Reproduced locally on two Lenovo units using current USB cloning station; suspect the USB duplicator firmware copies SMBIOS/UUID fields. Opening a vendor support case.

Vendor Support (Cloning vendor): Confirmed default duplicator model can copy full disk + system metadata unless 'Strip UUID/SMBIOS' option enabled; provided firmware v2.1.3 that includes 'randomize-smbios' flag.
Security (Auditing): Noted risk to assetdb integrity if hardware identifiers are duplicated; recommended temporary block on auto-activation of devices with identical UUIDs in assetdb.
Liam Chen: Deployed a script to detect duplicate SMBIOS UUID at first SCCM checkin and report to imaging queue (hotfix).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Cloning station copies SMBIOS/SMBIOS UUID fields, leading to multiple devices sharing same UUID and causing Microsoft Activation service to treat them as same device.
Checked SCCM hardware inventory: group of 6 devices showed identical SystemProduct and UUID after same depot run on 2026-01-09.
Ran activation trace: Office uses device identity + Azure AD device object to bind license; duplicate UUIDs cause token issuance to fail server-side (correlation id available in activation logs).
Tested vendor firmware v2.1.3 with 'randomize-smbios' flag — after reflash, new machines reported unique UUIDs and Office activated normally.

Alternative mitigation tested: Post-image PowerShell script that rewrites SMBIOS fields is not feasible from Windows userland; firmware-level change required or demand vendor to avoid copying SMBIOS metadata.
resolution: Applied multi-step fix: 1) Instructed depot vendor to reflash USB cloning stations to firmware v2.1.3 with 'randomize-smbios' enabled (effective 2026-01-15). 2) Added a pre-check to SCCM task sequence to detect duplicate SMBIOS UUID and stall task sequence with a diagnostic artifact uploaded to imaging queue. 3) For devices already issued, imaging team re-flashed affected units and re-ran provisioning; Office activation succeeded after re-provisioning. Post-mortem: updated depot runbook and added 'SMBIOS randomization verification' audit step. Case closed.
